title: Given a Scenario, Implement IPv4 and IPv6 Network Services

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Network services perform essential background work: assigning addresses, resolving names, validating DNS information, and synchronizing time for IPv4 and IPv6 systems.
bullets: DHCP reservations, scopes, leases, options, relay/IP helper, and exclusions
DNSSEC, DoH, DoT, and common DNS records
Forward/reverse, authoritative/non-authoritative, primary/secondary, and recursive DNS

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: When a host needs addressing, name resolution, or accurate time, identify the network service and configuration option that controls the required behavior.
bullets: Same address for the same client → Reservation

sections.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP)
paragraphs: DHCP automatically supplies IPv4 clients with an address, subnet information, default gateway, DNS servers, and other network settings.

entries.title: Scope
paragraphs: A DHCP scope defines the pool or range of addresses available for a particular network.
entries.memoryHook: Which addresses can DHCP hand out?

entries.title: Reservation
paragraphs: A reservation consistently assigns a particular DHCP address to a particular client, providing predictable addressing without manual client configuration.
entries.memoryHook: DHCP, but always the same address.

entries.title: Lease Time
paragraphs: Lease time controls how long a client may use an assigned address before renewal. Short leases suit rapidly changing clients; longer leases reduce renewal activity in stable environments.
entries.memoryHook: How long may the client keep it?

entries.title: Options
paragraphs: DHCP options provide extra settings such as the default gateway, DNS servers, and other network-specific parameters.

entries.title: Relay/IP Helper
paragraphs: A DHCP relay, often configured as an IP helper, forwards DHCP messages between subnets because routers do not normally forward the client's initial broadcasts.
entries.memoryHook: Client and DHCP server are on different subnets.

entries.title: Exclusions
paragraphs: An exclusion identifies addresses inside the network range that DHCP must not assign dynamically, protecting addresses used by routers, servers, printers, and infrastructure.
entries.memoryHook: Do not give these addresses out.

sections.callout: Pool → Scope. Same client/same address → Reservation. Keep out → Exclusion.

sections.title: Stateless Address Autoconfiguration (SLAAC)
paragraphs: SLAAC lets an IPv6 host form its own IPv6 address using information advertised by the local IPv6 network, without requiring a stateful DHCP server to assign the address.
sections.callout: Server-driven assignment → DHCP. IPv6 host self-configuration → SLAAC.

sections.title: DNS, DNSSEC, DoH, and DoT

entries.title: Domain Name System (DNS)
paragraphs: DNS resolves human-friendly names to network information such as IP addresses.

entries.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC)
paragraphs: DNSSEC cryptographically validates the authenticity and integrity of DNS data. Its primary purpose is trusting the answer, not encrypting the query.
entries.memoryHook: Can I trust this DNS answer?

entries.title: DNS over HTTPS (DoH)
paragraphs: DoH protects DNS queries by carrying them through HTTPS.

entries.title: DNS over TLS (DoT)
paragraphs: DoT protects DNS communication directly with TLS.

sections.callout: Trust the answer → DNSSEC. HTTPS transport → DoH. TLS transport → DoT.

sections.title: DNS Record Types

table.caption: Required Network+ DNS record recognition
rows: One name points to another name
DNS server responsible for a zone

sections.callout: A → IPv4. AAAA → IPv6. CNAME → Alias. MX → Mail. TXT → Text. NS → Nameserver. PTR → Reverse.

entries.title: Forward and Reverse Zones
paragraphs: A forward zone resolves a hostname to an IP address. A reverse zone uses PTR records to resolve an IP address back to a hostname.
entries.memoryHook: Name first → Forward. IP first → Reverse.

entries.title: Authoritative vs. Non-Authoritative
paragraphs: An authoritative answer comes from a DNS server responsible for the zone. A non-authoritative answer comes from another source, often cached data held by a resolver.
entries.memoryHook: Owns the answer vs. learned the answer.

entries.title: Primary vs. Secondary
paragraphs: A primary DNS zone holds the main writable copy. A secondary holds a replicated copy received from a primary.

entries.title: Recursive DNS
paragraphs: A recursive resolver contacts other DNS servers on the client's behalf until it finds the needed answer.
entries.memoryHook: Client asks once; resolver does the searching.

sections.title: Hosts File
paragraphs: A hosts file provides local, static hostname-to-IP mappings on one device and can resolve those entries without querying DNS.
sections.callout: One device and manual mapping → Hosts file. Central network name-resolution service → DNS.

sections.title: Time Protocols
paragraphs: Accurate time supports logging, authentication, certificates, troubleshooting, distributed systems, and security analysis.

entries.title: Network Time Protocol (NTP)
paragraphs: NTP provides general clock synchronization across networked devices.
entries.memoryHook: Keep everybody on the same clock.

entries.title: Precision Time Protocol (PTP)
paragraphs: PTP provides highly precise synchronization for environments where normal NTP precision is insufficient.
entries.memoryHook: When NTP is not precise enough.

entries.title: Network Time Security (NTS)
paragraphs: NTS adds authentication and protection to network time synchronization.

sections.callout: General time → NTP. High precision → PTP. Secure time → NTS.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: DHCP across a router → Relay/IP helper

entries.title: Reservation vs. Exclusion
paragraphs: Same client always receives the same DHCP address → Reservation. DHCP never dynamically issues an address → Exclusion.

entries.title: Scope vs. Lease
paragraphs: Pool of addresses → Scope. How long an assignment remains valid → Lease.

entries.title: DHCP vs. SLAAC
paragraphs: Server-driven assignment → DHCP. IPv6 self-configuration → SLAAC.

entries.title: DNSSEC vs. DoH vs. DoT
paragraphs: Validate DNS data → DNSSEC. Encrypt DNS with HTTPS → DoH. Encrypt DNS with TLS → DoT.

entries.title: A vs. AAAA
paragraphs: IPv4 → A. IPv6 → AAAA.

entries.title: CNAME vs. A
paragraphs: Alias to another hostname → CNAME. Hostname directly mapped to IPv4 → A.

entries.title: MX vs. NS
paragraphs: Mail server → MX. DNS server for the zone → NS.

entries.title: Forward vs. Reverse DNS
paragraphs: Name to address → Forward. Address to name → Reverse.

entries.title: Authoritative vs. Recursive
paragraphs: Owns the zone answer → Authoritative. Searches other servers for the client → Recursive.

entries.title: Primary vs. Secondary
paragraphs: Main writable zone → Primary. Replica → Secondary.

entries.title: Hosts File vs. DNS
paragraphs: Local static mapping → Hosts file. Central name-resolution service → DNS.

entries.title: NTP vs. PTP vs. NTS
paragraphs: General time → NTP. Precise time → PTP. Secure time → NTS.
